resources.summary: With a 4-month-old and $1,650 a month for two people, she is under 100% of the poverty line and qualifies for most major programs; realistically about $1,700-$2,000 a month in food, health coverage, child care and tax credits. Tomorrow: apply for SNAP and Children's Medicaid in one application at YourTexasBenefits.com, then call Texas WIC at 1-800-942-3678.

items.name: Child Care Scholarship (CCS, Texas CCDF subsidy - Workforce Solutions Gulf Coast)
items.why: Income far below the state limit and she works. Infant care slots are prioritized for low-income working parents.
items.value: Most of infant day care paid; small co-pay. Worth $600-$900/mo
steps: Call 2-1-1 and ask for Workforce Solutions child care services.
Apply online with Workforce Solutions Gulf Coast.
Submit 30 days of pay stubs and the baby's birth certificate.
Ask to be put on the waiting list if one exists.
items.verify_note: Could not confirm the current income limit or waitlist status online. Confirm with Workforce Solutions Gulf Coast.

items.name: Earned Income Tax Credit and Child Tax Credit (free help through VITA)
items.why: She works and has one qualifying child, so she can claim both credits even with no tax owed.
items.value: Roughly $4,000-$6,000 once a year as a refund
steps: Get the baby a Social Security number if not done.
Find a free VITA tax site by calling 2-1-1.
File a 2026 return even if income is low.
Ask the preparer to check both EITC and the Child Tax Credit.
documents: Social Security cards for her and baby
Bank account number for direct deposit
Last year's tax return if any
items.verify_note: Exact credit amounts depend on 2026 filing rules. A VITA volunteer can calculate them free.

items.name: Early Head Start (birth to age 3)
items.why: Early Head Start takes children under 3 from families at or below 100% of poverty. Her income is below that line.
items.value: Free infant care, home visits, developmental screening
steps: Call 2-1-1 and ask for Early Head Start near ZIP 77036.
Contact BakerRipley or Gulf Coast Community Services to apply.
Turn in proof of income and the birth certificate.
Accept a waiting list spot if offered.
documents: Proof of income or SNAP/TANF letter
items.verify_note: Could not confirm a Houston program's open slots. Local Early Head Start seats are limited; ask about the waiting list.
items.source_quote: A pregnant woman or a child is eligible if: (i) The family's income is equal to or below the poverty line

items.name: SNAP food benefits (Lone Star Card)
items.why: Texas allows gross income up to 165% of poverty; for two people that is about $2,909 a month. She earns $1,650.
items.value: Up to $546/mo for a household of 2; likely $300-$450
steps: Create an account at YourTexasBenefits.com.
Apply for SNAP and Medicaid in the same form.
Upload pay stubs and ID.
Answer the phone interview call from HHSC.
documents: Rent or lease and utility bills
items.verify_note: Benefit amount depends on rent and child care costs. Report them to raise the award.
items.source_quote: gross income below or equal to 165 percent Federal Poverty

items.name: Children's Medicaid / CHIP for the baby
items.why: Babies under age 1 qualify at roughly 198-203% of poverty in Texas. Her income is near 94% of poverty.
items.value: Free doctor visits, shots, prescriptions for the baby
steps: Apply at YourTexasBenefits.com in the same form as SNAP.
Choose a STAR health plan when approved.
Pick a pediatrician close to 77036.
Book the 6-month well-baby check.
items.verify_note: Could not confirm the exact 2026 income chart on an official page. Adult Medicaid in Texas is much stricter; ask about Healthy Texas Women for herself.

items.name: Texas WIC
items.why: The baby is under 5 and her income is under the WIC limit. SNAP or Medicaid approval also makes her income eligible.
items.value: Free formula or food, plus $50-$100/mo in food benefits
steps: Call 1-800-942-3678 for the clinic near 77036.
Book an appointment and bring the baby.
Bring proof of income and address.
Load the WIC card and shop at WIC stores.
documents: Medicaid or SNAP letter if any
items.verify_note: Current posted limit for a household of 2 is about $3,337 a month. Confirm at the clinic.
items.source_quote: Applicants on Medicaid, TANF or SNAP may already meet the income eligibility guidelines for WIC. Households with income up to 185% of the federal poverty level are eligible.

items.name: CEAP utility help (LIHEAP in Texas, run by BakerRipley)
items.why: Harris County residents at low income can get electric or gas bills paid. Applications are taken in person by appointment.
items.value: Several hundred dollars toward past-due electric bills
steps: Call 2-1-1 or 713-696-7900 for an appointment.
Gather the last electric bill and all income proof.
Attend the in-person appointment.
Ask about crisis help if a shut-off notice exists.
documents: Social Security cards for all in home
Most recent electric or gas bill
Proof of income for past 30 days
items.verify_note: Texas does not post this application online and funds run out. Call early in the month.
items.source_quote: Eligibility for CEAP is calculated at 150% of Federal Poverty Income Guidelines.

items.name: Houston Lone Star Diaper Bank / Houston Diaper Bank
items.why: Houston diaper banks give free diapers and wipes to low-income families with an infant. No income paperwork at most sites.
items.value: About 50-75 free diapers a month, worth $40-$60
steps: Check Diaper Day dates at lonestardiaperbank.org.
Call 2-1-1 for the nearest partner site to 77036.
Bring ID and the baby's size.
Ask about free wipes and formula too.
documents: Baby's birth certificate or clinic card
items.verify_note: Distribution days and partner sites change monthly. Confirm before traveling.
items.source_quote: Our diaper bank offers relief to families by providing free diapers and baby products

items.name: Houston Food Bank pantry network
items.why: Pantries serve anyone in need. Most sites in 77036 need only ID and an address, no income test.
items.value: Free groceries weekly, roughly $40-$80 of food
steps: Call 2-1-1 for the closest pantry to 77036.
Check the pantry's open hours before going.
Bring bags and a way to carry food.
Ask if they stock baby food and formula.
items.verify_note: Hours vary by site. Some pantries limit visits to once a month.

items.name: Lifeline phone and internet discount
items.why: Income at or below 135% of poverty qualifies, about $2,381 a month for two. SNAP or Medicaid also qualifies her.
items.value: $9.25 off phone or internet each month; some plans become free
steps: Apply at CheckLifeline.org.
Upload the SNAP or Medicaid approval letter.
Pick a Lifeline provider after approval.
Recertify once a year.
items.verify_note: Only one Lifeline benefit per household. Texas also has a state phone discount; ask the provider.
items.source_quote: A consumer can qualify for the Lifeline benefit if their income is 135% or less than the federal poverty guidelines

items.name: 2-1-1 Texas (United Way HELPLINE)
items.why: Free referral line for anyone in Texas. It finds rent help, pantries, child care and baby items near her ZIP.
items.value: Free. Opens the door to local rent, utility and baby-goods help
steps: Dial 2-1-1 and pick English.
Say the ZIP code 77036 and what is needed.
Ask for Buy Nothing or free baby gear groups.
Write down each agency name and phone.

items.name: TANF cash help
items.why: Texas TANF is for families with almost no income. Earnings of $1,650 a month are well above the budget test.
items.value: Up to about $300/mo cash for a parent and one child, if approved
steps: Apply at YourTexasBenefits.com only if work hours stop.
Check the TANF box on the same SNAP application.
Ask about the one-time $1,000 crisis payment.
Report any job loss right away.
items.verify_note: Worth applying only if income drops. Asset limit is about $1,000.
items.source_quote: Families who can get TANF cash help have little to no money or don’t have a way to get money.
